To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students who perceive they are supported by their teachers, are more engaged and more likely to achieve academically.
students in schools with higher levels of teacher support for learning are more likely to report higher levels of academic achievement and engagement.

1) teacher support, as measured by teacher-student relationships, is a significant factor in student engagement and achievement in high school, 2) student engagement, as measured by student perceptions of their school experience, is a significant predictor of student achievement, and 3) teacher support and student engagement are related to the social and emotional climate of the school.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the school environment influences student engagement and achievement and what can be done to improve the school environment for students.
the impact of teacher support on student engagement and achievement.
the relationship between teacher support, student engagement, and student achievement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a positive school climate and teacher-student relationships contribute significantly to student achievement.
the quality of the relationship between teachers and students has a positive effect on student achievement and engagement.
student achievement is a result of the interaction between the student and his or her school environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students are more likely to succeed when they are supported by caring adults.
relationships matter.
the more students are connected to school and the more support they receive, the more they are engaged in school, and the higher the achievement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers and other adults in schools can make a difference in student achievement.
teachers and other school staff can have a significant impact on student learning.
